_comment: The Claude Code hook contract this recipe is written against, transcribed from the docs.
It is the compatibility tier of the gate: the test next to this file asserts that every
field hook.py reads and every field it returns appears here, and that the payload shapes
below are the ones the demo feeds the hook. Re-fetch the three sources on the week of
publication; a change here is what tells us the recipe needs updating.

optional_input_fields.agent_id: Unique identifier when the hook fires inside a subagent
optional_input_fields.agent_type: Agent name (the frontmatter `name`) when using --agent or inside a subagent

subagent_start.output_note: JSON output is ignored for this event; exit 2 shows stderr to the user only and the subagent still spawns.

exit_codes.0: Success. Stdout is read for JSON control fields.
exit_codes.2: Blocking error on events that support blocking. On PreToolUse: blocks the tool call. Stderr becomes the blocking reason.

exit_zero_without_json: Normal permission flow applies (not an approval).
matcher_note: A handler with no `matcher` runs for every tool call — which is what a fail-closed recorder needs.

tool_resolution.tools_omitted: Subagent inherits every tool available to subagents.
tool_resolution.disallowed_only: Subagent gets the default pool minus those tools.
tool_resolution.both: disallowedTools is applied first, then tools is resolved against the remainder; a tool in both is removed.
tool_resolution.agent_syntax: Agent(worker, researcher) in `tools` allowlists which subagents may be spawned.

transcripts.format: JSONL, one JSON object per line
transcripts.note: Transcripts record what happened. The docs describe no hash chain, signature or anchor over them, so they are not something a third party can check for completeness or alteration on its own. That is the gap this recipe fills; it is not a criticism of what transcripts are for.
